subject: Post-demo readout: recommended models, benchmark links & trial ops
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@orbitalpay.com>, Raj Patel <raj@orbitalpay.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo readout: recommended models, benchmark links & trial ops

Hi Emma / Raj — thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get a short evaluation sprint running next week.

1) Readout / recommended models
- Baseline you showed: Orbital internal QA model (v2.3-prop) — good coverage on domain-specific tokens but higher latency.
- Redwood recommended candidates (open variants we propose you trial):
  * rw-open-13B-q4f — strong token efficiency, expected token cost ~35–40% lower than your baseline in our sample runs.
  * rw-open-30B-pt — better long-form coherence on transactional prompts; slightly higher latency but better recall on multi-turn contexts.
  * rw-open-13B-kv — same architecture as first candidate but with KV-cache optimization for short-turn chat flows (helps lower P95).

Acceptance guidance (what we’ll use to evaluate parity):
- Latency: P95 generation latency <= 200ms for typical 64-token completions (edge: 250ms OK with trade-offs).
- Quality: top-line accuracy / correctness on your test set within 3% of the proprietary baseline on the target task (intent extraction + entity accuracy).
- Safety/regressions: hallucination rate (as measured by your oracle checks) not to increase by more than 1 percentage point.

2) Benchmarks & artifacts attached
- Attached: RW_eval-plan_v1.pdf — contains the benchmark suite we propose, prompt bundles, and evaluation scripts.
- Drive folder with raw logs + scripts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cEvalPlan
- HubSpot deal record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/OP-2026-091

3) Trial configuration & ops asks
- Proposed trial: 2-week scoped trial covering (a) intent/entity extraction bundle, (b) one multi-turn support flow.
- We will provide pre-built promptpacks and a short runner script; we’ll need a technical contact to share sample payloads and network egress requirements.
- Runtime constraints we discussed: token-budget target, per-request max tokens 512, keep-alive / KV cache enabled for multi-turn tests.

4) Commercial notes (high level)
- Trial is free; if open models meet acceptance gates we’ll discuss committed pricing for Dedicated or Redwood Hosted with a conversion path.

Next steps
- Emma / Raj: confirm the two-week window that works for you (we suggested Oct 6 start).
- Please upload two representative prompt files to the Drive folder or attach them here (we recommend one short-turn batch and one multi-turn session log).
- I’ll loop in Prioym and Vivek to scope the infra + observability runbook.

Attachments: RW_eval-plan_v1.pdf (evaluation plan, promptpacks, scripts)

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Thanks Lauren — this looks great and matches my notes. A couple of quick clarifications before we lock the start date: 

1) Token cost profile: can you share an estimated cost / token delta for rw-open-13B-q4f vs the baseline on our sample bundle? That’ll feed into our internal TCO ask.
2) Data residency: for the Hosted option, does Redwood store logs outside of our region? We need to confirm data stays in our US region for the trial.
3) Runtime behavior: you mentioned KV-cache; will the trial preserve session KV across restarts for the multi-turn flow, or is it best-effort?

I attached a small sample of our prompt bundles (orbital-sample-prompts.csv) — short and long examples. Happy to start Oct 6 if we can get the token-cost sketch and a short runbook for infra.

Thanks,

emma.li@orbitalpay.com | +1 650-555-8899

-----Original Message-----
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@orbitalpay.com>, Raj Patel <raj@orbitalpay.com>
Cc: Prioym Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo readout: recommended models, benchmark links & trial ops

Emma — great, thanks for the sample prompts. Quick answers inline below and then an ask for the trial kickoff: 

1) Token-cost sketch
- Early estimates (based on your sample bundle of ~1.2M tokens processed in our runner):
  * rw-open-13B-q4f: ~0.62x token cost vs your baseline (we estimate ~38% lower).
  * rw-open-30B-pt: ~0.95x token cost but higher quality for long-form recall tasks.
- I’ll attach a CSV with per-prompt cost estimates in a follow-up (we’ll run the exact samples overnight and post results to the Drive).

2) Data residency / logs
- Hosted mode stores logs in the region you select for the tenant; for the trial we can pin to US-West and configure retention to 7 days for debug logs. We do not export customer logs outside the selected region by default.

3) KV-cache behavior
- The rw-open-13B-kv trial variant will persist session KV for the lifetime of a container; best-effort across restarts unless you choose Dedicated where we can guarantee sticky routing. For the trial we’ll enable keep-alives and session affinity to minimize cache misses.

Trial kickoff: can we schedule a 30-minute technical kickoff with Raj (your SRE) on Oct 6, 10:00am PT? I’ll bring the test runner and Prioym will own the experiment config.

Internal ask (Prioym / Vivek):
- Prioym: please prepare an initial runner config for the three candidate variants (13B-q4f, 13B-kv, 30B-pt) with target batch sizes and a short runbook for capturing P95 latency and token-cost breakdown.
- Vivek: we’ll need an observability template (dashboard + trace links) and a short checklist for data-residency controls to include in the trial runbook.

I’ll schedule the kickoff once Raj confirms availability.

Thanks,
Lauren

-----Original Message-----
From: Prioym Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 18:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo readout: recommended models, benchmark links & trial ops

Copying my notes here for the runbook we discussed — pushing a short config so we can be ready for Oct 6 kickoff if scheduled: 

- Runner config (initial):
  * Variants: rw-open-13B-q4f (cpu quant), rw-open-13B-kv (kv-enabled), rw-open-30B-pt (fp16).
  * Batch size: 8 for short-turn flows, 4 for long-form to avoid head-of-line blocking.
  * Max concurrent sessions: 120 for the trial account, token cap per request 512.
  * Autoscaling: conservative for trial (min 1 container per variant, max 4) to control token spend.

- Metrics to capture:
  * P50 / P95 / P99 latency per variant (generation phase only).
  * Tokens produced per request and token cost breakdown (model compute + infra).
  * Failure rate and any hallucination flags (we’ll tie to your oracle checks).

- Quick troubleshooting notes:
  * If P95 > 250ms on rw-open-13B-q4f, reduce batch to 4 or pin to a GPU-optimized instance and re-run.
  * For multi-turn flows, enforce session affinity header (x-rw-session) to keep KV localized.

I’ll drop the runner manifest and a minimal terraform snippet into the Drive folder by end of day.

— Prioym
